ceiling_directive: Prove a uniform, data-measurable same-class upper bound at \(m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\), thereby turning the oracle balance into a genuine minimax characterization on the stated polynomial-boundary transport class.
improvement_directive: Establish held-out localization for the capped RiCOT weights and frontier-order bounds for both \(\overline B_X\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i^2\) at \(h_n\); use these bounds to prove that the executable spliced estimator has root risk at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\).
critique: The note proves a substantive three-regime minimax lower bound, including the critical logarithm, but it proves no matching upper bound for any data-measurable estimator. The matching bias–standard-deviation calculation is law-indexed and oracle, so it does not establish attainability of the minimax rate. The executable RiCOT construction supplies only an algebraic linear representation and a potentially very wide finite-sample coverage certificate, with no stochastic control of its bias radius, coefficient norm, risk, or expected interval length. Consequently the advertised frontier remains an impossibility phase diagram paired with an oracle benchmark, rather than a settled minimax frontier, which keeps the contribution below the field floor.
